checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does parse_deposit_requests properly filter logs by topic presence and signature hash before processing?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the parse_deposit_requests function in the EL implementation. 2. Verify that the function checks len(log.topics) > 0 BEFORE accessing log.topics[0]. 3. Verify that the function compares log.topics[0] against DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH. 4. Attempt to submit a transaction that causes the deposit contract to emit a log with empty topics array - verify the log is skipped. 5. Attempt to submit a transaction that causes a log with log.topics[0] != DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH from the deposit contract address - verify the log is skipped. 6. Verify that logs with empty topics do not cause an index-out-of-bounds error or crash. 7. Test edge cases: single topic that doesn't match, multiple topics where first doesn't match, anonymous events from deposit contract.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0009, Trust Boundary: tb-002. This property guards the EL node from processing non-deposit event logs as deposit requests. A crafted transaction could cause the deposit contract to emit logs with unexpected topics. If topic filtering is missing, non-deposit events could be processed as deposits, causing incorrect requests hash computation and consensus divergence between EL implementations.

checklist.title: Verify empty topics array handling in parse_deposit_requests does not cause crashes or undefined behavior
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Craft a block containing a receipt with a log from DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS that has an empty topics array (len(log.topics) == 0). 2. Submit the block via P2P to the target EL node. 3. Verify the node does NOT crash, panic, or exhibit undefined behavior. 4. Verify the node correctly skips this log and continues processing. 5. Verify no deposit request is generated from this log. 6. Compare behavior across multiple EL implementations (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) - all must skip the log identically.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0009, Supporting check for actor-el-node. Accessing log.topics[0] without first checking len(log.topics) > 0 would cause an index-out-of-bounds error in most languages. This is a classic off-by-one/bounds-check vulnerability pattern.

checklist.title: Verify that logs with non-matching first topic from deposit contract are correctly filtered out
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Deploy or identify a scenario where the deposit contract emits a log with topics[0] != DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH (e.g., if the deposit contract has other events, or via a proxy/delegate call pattern). 2. Create a transaction that triggers this non-deposit event from the deposit contract address. 3. Include this transaction in a block and submit via P2P. 4. Verify the parse_deposit_requests function skips this log entirely. 5. Verify the deposit_requests accumulator does NOT include any data from this log. 6. Compute the expected requests hash (excluding this log) and verify the EL produces the correct hash. 7. Differential test: compare output across Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon - all must produce identical requests hash.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0009, Supporting check for actor-deposit-contract. If a log with log.address == DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS but log.topics[0] != DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH is processed as a deposit, the extracted data would be garbage, causing consensus divergence.
